{{short description|German sociologist and statistician}}
'''Frauke Kreuter''' is a German [[sociologist]] and [[statistician]]. She is a professor of the [[Joint Program in Survey Methodology]] (JPSM) of the [[University of Maryland, College Park]] and a professor in [[statistics]] and [[data science]] at [[LMU Munich]], Germany. Her research in [[survey methodology]] includes work on [[sampling error]] and [[observational error]].

==Biography==
Kreuter earned a [[Diplom#Germany|diploma]] in [[sociology]] from the [[University of Mannheim]] in 1996. She received her doctorate (Dr. rer. soc.) in 2001 from the [[University of Konstanz]] under the supervision of {{Interlanguage link multi|Rainer Schnell|de}}. After postdoctoral research and an adjunct position at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]], she moved to [[Maryland]] in 2004 and joined [[Joint Program in Survey Methodology|JPSM]] as an assistant professor. From 2010 to 2014 she was University Professor of Statistics at [[LMU Munich]], while maintaining her position at the University of Maryland as an associate professor. She also became head of the Statistical Methods Research Department at the [[Institute for Employment Research (IAB)]] in [[Nuremberg]], Germany in 2010. In 2014 she was promoted to full professor at [[Maryland]] and moved her German position to the [[University of Mannheim]]. From 2016 to 2020, she was director of [[Joint Program in Survey Methodology|JPSM]] in [[Maryland]]. She also founded the International Program for Survey and Data Science (IPSDS) at LMU Munich, Germany, and co-founded the Coleridge Initiative.<ref name=":1" />

==Awards and honors==
Kreuter was the 2013 winner of the Gertrude Cox Award, given jointly by the [[Washington Statistical Society]] and [[RTI International]].<ref>[https://jpsm.umd.edu/news/frauke-kreuter-wins-2013-gertrude-cox-award-presented-washington-statistical-society-wss-and Frauke Kreuter wins 2013 Gertrude Cox Award presented by the Washington Statistical Society (WSS) and RTI International] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160919220805/https://jpsm.umd.edu/news/frauke-kreuter-wins-2013-gertrude-cox-award-presented-washington-statistical-society-wss-and |date=2016-09-19 }}, JPSM, Univ. of Maryland, retrieved 2016-07-14.</ref>
In 2014 she was elected as a [[Fellow]] of the [[American Statistical Association]] "for outstanding contributions to research in the field of [[survey methodology]]; for excellence in mentoring of junior researchers in [[social statistics]] and [[survey methodology]]; and for extensive international research collaborations."<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.amstat.org/newsroom/pressreleases/2014_ASAFellows.pdf|title=ASA Honors 63 New Fellows|publisher=[[American Statistical Association]]|date=June 11, 2014|accessdate=2016-07-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304054602/http://www.amstat.org/newsroom/pressreleases/2014_ASAFellows.pdf|archive-date=March 4, 2016|url-status=dead}}.</ref> She was awarded the [[Warren Mitofsky Innovators Award]] of the [[American Association for Public Opinion Research]] in 2020, and served as the association's president in 2025.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Sha |first=Mandy |date=2025-03-02 |title=Expanding the Reach of Scientific Communication: Tools, Motivation, and Recommendations |url=https://www.surveypractice.org/article/127308-expanding-the-reach-of-scientific-communication-tools-motivation-and-recommendations |journal=Survey Practice |language=en |volume=19 Special Issue |pages=1–8 |doi=10.29115/SP-2024-0032 |doi-access=free}}</ref><ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Chair of Statistics and Data Science in Social Sciences and the Humanities (SODA) & Deputy Head of Department |url=https://www.stat.lmu.de/soda/en/team/contact-page/frauke-kreuter-825909f7.html |access-date=2025-06-27 |website=www.stat.lmu.de |language=en}}</ref>
